chart.title: Sample Launch Chart
columns: How the Conflict Develops or Intensifies
rows: Langston focuses on memories of mother and Alabama. Not focusing on Chicago because he is so sad over his mother's death and missing his old life.

Langston struggles even more to fit in at school because instead of paying attention and focusing on starting a new life in Chicago, he constantly thinks about his sadness over his mother's death and life in Alabama he misses.
Bullies at school are now violent and hit him. Hint that they will hurt him more.
Conflict intensifies as Langston is afraid to go to school and cannot escape to his memories of Alabama and his mother. Makes Langston feel miserable.
Cannot share the bullying with his only parent—his dad—or the only neighbor who knows him—Miss Fulton. Teachers do not protect Langston from bullies.

Langston's loneliness intensifies as he feels he does not have anyone to help him, even when he is in fear of his physical safety. Conflict develops because not only does Langston feel isolated, he starts to feel hopeless that the upcoming days at school will get worse.

teaching_point: Fiction readers know that a story's conflict changes as the narrative progresses. They track the conflict as the plot progresses and ask themselves, "How does the conflict develop and intensify?"
